You are teammate "migrator-a" on a 3-person team (teammates: migrator-a, migrator-b, migrator-c; lead: "main"). Repo: <run-dir> (Node ESM, tests via `node --test`).

Goal: migrate the service modules in src/services/ from callback-style db access (src/db.js `query`/`update`) to the repository pattern (src/repositories/*.js, promise-based classes). Read .claude/skills/migrate-module/SKILL.md for the mapping table and steps.

Workflow:
1. Call TaskList. Claim the lowest-ID task that is pending, unowned and unblocked by calling TaskUpdate with owner "migrator-a" and status "in_progress". Then TaskGet it to confirm you own it (another teammate may have raced you — if the owner isn't you, pick another).
2. Migrate that module and its test file in tests/. If a table has no repository class, create one in src/repositories/ following the existing shape; if a needed method is missing from an existing repository, add it (don't change existing method behavior). Converting exports to promises changes callers: src/api/routes.js calls user-service, order-service and payment-service. Update the call sites for YOUR module's exports in routes.js with small targeted Edit calls only (other teammates edit the same file). 5. Repeat from step 1 until no unclaimed unblocked module task remains. Task #5 (full suite) is blocked on the four migrations; if it becomes unblocked and unclaimed, you may claim it and run `npm test`, reporting failures to the relevant owners.
Don't commit. Respond to messages from teammates promptly.

Final reply: for each task you owned — module, files changed, repositories created/extended, test command and exact pass/fail counts, and any messages you sent/received about cross-module effects.
</teammate-message>

file.content:
---
name: migrate-module
description: Migrates one service module from callback-style database access to the matching repository class, then runs that module's tests. Use when the user names a single service file to migrate. Handles exactly one module per invocation.
---

# Repository pattern migration

The mapping table from callback call to repository method:

| Callback call in a service | Repository method |
|---|---|
| `query('users', u => u.deleted_at === null, cb)` | `UserRepository.findActive()` |
| `query('users', u => u.id === id, cb)` | `UserRepository.findById(id)` |
| `update('users', id, { deleted_at }, cb)` | `UserRepository.softDelete(id, when)` |
| `query('orders', o => o.user_id === id ..., cb)` | `OrderRepository.findByUser(id)` |
| `query('orders', o => o.status === 'paid' ..., cb)` | `OrderRepository.findPaid()` |

Steps:

1. Read the target service file and its test file.
2. Replace every direct `query`/`update` import and call with the matching repository method.
3. Convert the exported functions to return promises. Update the test file to await them.
4. Run only that module's tests: `node --test tests/<module>.test.js`.
5. Stop after three failed attempts and report what blocked you.

`payments` has no repository yet. If the target is `payment-service.js`, create
`src/repositories/payment-repository.js` following the shape of the other two.

- **routes.js:** I made two targeted edits to the `/users` and `/users/:id` handlers. They now call the promise and pass the result to the callback, the same pattern migrator-b used.
